<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th colspan="4">NAME</th>
<th colspan="5">Menu Text</th>
<th>Type</th>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<th colspan="2"></th>
<th colspan="8">Entry Action / Exit Action / Lock / Routine</th>
</tr>
<tr class="header">
<th colspan="2">DESCR:</th>
<th colspan="8">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM 2237 DEL</td>
<td colspan="4">Delete 2237 Request from Supply Worksheet File</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">DEL2237^PRCHRPT3</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">This option It removed the 2237 from file 443 but left the electronic signature information in File 410, making the 2237 inaccessible to the service and to A&amp;MM. 2237s with status of Returned to Service no longer appear on the Outstanding 2237 Report, so the option is no longer needed.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS ADD</td>
<td colspan="4">Create Code Sheet (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">CCS^PRCFALOG</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows user to create a LOG, GSA or DLA code sheet, using the pre-defined edit templates that prompt for specific fields. It does not pre-load any data from Purchase Orders, Requisitions or Receiving Reports.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS ADD TO BATCH</td>
<td colspan="4">Add Code Sheet to Printed Batch (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">ADD^PRCFALOG</td>
<td>LOCK:</td>
<td colspan="2">PRCHPM CS TRANSMIT</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows user to add a code sheet to a batch, after the batch has already been "Batched and Printed," but before it has been transmitted to Austin. <em>Note:</em> If a code sheet has already been assigned to a batch, it must be removed from the original batch before it can be assigned to a new batch. The option also adjusts the Batch Header Code Sheet to account for the addition.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS BATCH &amp; PRINT</td>
<td colspan="4">Batch and Print Code Sheet (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">BATCH^PRCFALOG</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows PPM to print the actual LOG, GSA and DLA code sheets which have been created and signed, but not yet released to Austin. This is the final step that must be done before the actual transmission.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS BATCH MANAGEMENT</td>
<td colspan="4">Batch Management Menu (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>M</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Contains options allowing user to print and transmit LOG, GSA and DLA code sheets to Austin, and to perform other tasks needed to maintain and track the batches.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS CREATE (ACQUISITION)</td>
<td colspan="4">Acquisitions Code Sheets Generation (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">EN1^PRCHEC</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows PPM to generate LOG 1, GSA or DLA code sheets for Acquisitions, either for Posted Stock orders, or Requisitions from Government Sources. This option is generally used only for doing Posted Stock orders for non-government sources, since government source code sheets are generated during the normal processing of the Requisition.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS CREATE (DEPOT REC)</td>
<td colspan="4">Depot Receiving Code Sheet Generation</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">EN2^PRCHDEP3</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Used only by HINES to generate code sheets to LOG for items which have been received into Depot Stock. (Trans 431/434)</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS CREATE (DEPOT)</td>
<td colspan="4">Depot Due-in Code Sheet Generation</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">EN1^PRCHDEP3</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Used only by HINES to create Due-in LOG code sheets (transaction code 401).</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS CREATE (ISSUES)</td>
<td colspan="4">Issues Code Sheet Generation (LOG)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">PRCHED</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Builds a Issue Request Log code sheet for a selected transaction and allows the code sheet to be edited and set up for transmission.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS CREATE (RECEIVING)</td>
<td colspan="4">Receiving Code Sheets Generation (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">EN2^PRCHEC</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows PPM to generate LOG, GSA or DLA code sheets for receiving.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS CREATE/EDIT MENU</td>
<td colspan="4">Create or Edit Code Sheets Manually (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>M</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">EN2^PRCHEC</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows user to create or edit LOG, GSA or DLA code sheets manually (<em>i.e.</em>, those code sheets other than normal Receiving, Acquisitions or Issues, which are built from existing IFCAP data).</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS DELETE</td>
<td colspan="4">Delete Existing Code Sheet (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">DCS^PRCFALOG</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows PPM agent to delete a LOG, DLA or GSA code sheet before it is actually released to Austin.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS DELETE FROM BATCH</td>
<td colspan="4">Delete Code Sheet from Printed Batch (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">DELETE^PRCFALOG</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows user to remove a code sheet from a batch prior to transmission and it adjusts the Batch Header Code Sheet accordingly. This option must be used first when moving a code sheet from one batch to another.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS EDIT</td>
<td colspan="4">Edit Code Sheet (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">ECS^PRCFALOG</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows user to edit a LOG, GSA or DLA code sheet that was created using the "Create Code Sheet (LOG/GSA/DLA)" option (PRCHPM CS ADD). It uses the pre-defined edit templates that prompt for specific fields. It does not pre-load any data from Purchase Orders, Requisitions or Receiving Reports.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS EDIT</td>
<td colspan="4">Edit Code Sheet (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">ECS^PRCFALOG</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows user to edit a LOG, GSA or DLA code sheet that was created using the "Create Code Sheet (LOG/GSA/DLA)" option (PRCHPM CS ADD). It uses the pre-defined edit templates that prompt for specific fields. It does not pre-load any data from Purchase Orders, Requisitions or Receiving Reports.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS EDIT KEYPUNCHED CS</td>
<td colspan="4">Edit Keypunched Code Sheet (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">EKCS^PRCFALOG</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows user to directly edit the code of any code sheet without regard to the data stored in the code sheet fields. If used on a code sheet prepared normally, that code sheet becomes un-editable through normal means.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS INQUIRY TRANS/BATCH</td>
<td colspan="4">Inquiry to Batch/Transmission</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">INQUIRY^PRCFALOG</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Displays all information contained in the LOG Transmission Record file.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS KEYPUNCH</td>
<td colspan="4">Keypunch a Code Sheet (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">KCS^PRCFALOG</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows a PPM person to enter a code sheet manually, when all else fails.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS KEYPUNCH MENU</td>
<td colspan="4">Keypunch (direct entry) Menu (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>M</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows user to use the terminal as a keypunch machine to create LOG, GSA or DLA code sheets.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS MAIN MENU</td>
<td colspan="4">LOG/GSA/DLA Code Sheets Menu</td>
<td>M</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">This menu allows the creation, editing and printing of either LOG 1, GSA (which also are transmitted to LOG), and DLA code sheets by PPM.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS MODIFY BATCH PRI.</td>
<td colspan="4">Modify Batch Priority (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">MBP^PRCFALOG</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows a PPM person to assign a higher (2) or lower (4) batch priority to a code sheet. This can be used to insure that a certain code sheet will be transmitted ahead of or after others.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS PURGE</td>
<td colspan="4">Purge Code Sheets (LOG/GSA/DLA)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">PURGE^PRCFALOG</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9">Allows user to delete LOG/GSA/DLA code sheets from the code sheet file, which have been transmitted to Austin or DLA and which exceed a selectable number of days in age.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCHPM CS PURGE ALL</td>
<td colspan="4">Purge All Code Sheets</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3">ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="3">PURGE2^PRCFALOG</td>
<td colspan="4"></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3">DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7"><p>Allows user to delete all code sheets from the code sheet file, which have been transmitted to</p>
<p>Austin or DLA and which exceed a selectable number of days in age.</p></td>
</tr>

<span id="_Ref106418949" class="anchor"></span>Table 6.33. Option List (PRCP A — PRCPLO CLO)

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 10%" />
<col style="width: 0%" />
<col style="width: 34%" />
<col style="width: 0%" />
<col style="width: 17%" />
<col style="width: 9%" />
<col style="width: 19%" />
<col style="width: 8%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th colspan="3">NAME</th>
<th colspan="4">Menu Text</th>
<th>Type</th>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<th colspan="2"></th>
<th colspan="6">Entry Action / Exit Action / Lock / Routine</th>
</tr>
<tr class="header">
<th colspan="2">DESCR:</th>
<th colspan="6">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP ABBREVIATED ITEM REPORT</td>
<td colspan="3">Abbreviated Item Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRAIR</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Prints the Abbreviated Item Report. Report includes the item master number, description, NSN (for Warehouse), unit per issue, quantity on-hand, main storage location, and additional storage locations. The Warehouse will have the option to select specific item NSNs to display, and the report is sorted by NSN. The Primary and Secondary will have the option to select specific group categories to display, and the report is sorted by group category and description.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP ADJUSTMENT VOUCHER RECAP</td>
<td colspan="3">Adjustment Voucher Recap</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRADJ</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7"><p>Prints the Adjustment Voucher Recap. The Recap includes all adjustments to the inventory point for the specified month and year. The report will print the item master number, description, NSN (for Warehouse), and unit per issue. The report will break out each transaction register entry and print the reference number, transaction number, date of adjustment, adjustment units, quantity adjusted, value adjusted, selling value, fund control point, reason code, and user.</p>
<p>The inventory points will have the option to specify the month and year for adjustments. The warehouse report is sorted by NSN, while the report for the Primary and Secondary is sorted by description.</p>
<p>The user has the option to print a summary of the report data. By printing the summary, the report will not display each item and transaction register entry. It will only print a summary of account code adjustments broken out by positive and negative adjustments.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP AUTOGENERATE PRIM/ WAREHOUSE</td>
<td colspan="3">Auto-generate Orders</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPAGP0</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7"><p>Auto-generates a Primary or Warehouse inventory point Repetitive Item List (RIL). The auto-generation will use the selected group categories and vendors (stored in the mandatory or suggested source field in the primary and warehouse inventory points) for selecting the items. When an item's available quantity (quantity on hand plus quantity due-in minus quantity due-out) falls below or equal to the standard reorder point, the item will be ordered. When an item's available quantity falls below or equal to the optional reorder point, the item will be ordered if there are other items for the same vendor which are being ordered due to the available quantity</p>
<p>falling below the standard reorder point (if items only fall below the optional order point for a vendor, the order will not be generated).</p>
<p>The quantity to order is the difference between the available quantity and the normal stock level. Conversion factors (warehouse to primary, vendor to primary, or vendor to warehouse), vendor minimal issue quantity, and vendor issue multiple also factor into the total quantity of an item to order.</p>
<p>At completion of auto-generation, a series of reports can be generated. Each item in the inventory point will appear on one of the reports. This will aid in determining why an item was or was not ordered.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP AUTOMATIC LEVEL SETTER</td>
<td colspan="3">Automatic Level Setter</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRALS</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Produces a report that shows the current inventory levels versus the IFCAP-estimated levels. A user who has the manager key for the inventory point will have the option to automatically update the current levels to the estimated levels. The Primary and Secondary inventory point users will have the option to select specific group categories to display.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP AVAILABILITY LISTING</td>
<td colspan="3">Availability Listing</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRAVL</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7"><p>Produces the Availability Listing. The report includes the item master number, description, NSN, unit per issue, group category, quantity on-hand, quantity due-in, quantity due-out, reorder point, issue multiple, average unit cost, total value, and whether the item is set to "kill when zero." The Warehouse will have the option to sort by the selected NSN or account code, and the report is sorted by account code and NSN. The Primary will have the option to select specific group categories to display, and the report is sorted by group category and description.</p>
<p>The user has the option to print a summary of the report data. By printing the summary, the report will not display each item. In the Warehouse inventory point, the inventory value by account code will be summarized. In the Primary and Secondary inventory points, the inventory value by group category will be summarized.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP CATALOG/ORDER FORM PRINT</td>
<td colspan="3">Order Form</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRCAT</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Prints a catalog of items, which a distribution point can use for ordering and restocking its inventory point.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP CC ASSEMBLE</td>
<td colspan="3">Assemble Case Cart</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPCASC</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Used to build selected case carts by the case cart definition (which describes the items and quantities which are used in building the case cart). The user will have the option to select the number of case carts to build. After selecting the number, a screen display will show the current quantity on-hand and new quantity on-hand (after building) for the items which make up the case cart definition. The new quantity on-hand is calculated by subtracting the current quantity on-hand by the quantity needed for disposable items (reusable items are not removed from the inventory point during assembly). If any item's new quantity on-hand falls below zero, a warning message will be displayed on the screen.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP CC DEFINITION REPORT</td>
<td colspan="3">Case Cart Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPCRDC</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Produces the Case Cart Report. The report lists selected case carts displaying the items and quantities needed to assemble the case cart. Includes the items needed, description, quantity needed, whether the item is reusable or disposable, mandatory source vendor for reordering, catalog number for the mandatory source, and storage location.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP CC DISASSEMBLE</td>
<td colspan="3">Disassemble Case Cart</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPCDIC</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Used to disassemble (break down) case carts and return the individual disposable items back to stock. When a case cart is disassembled, the quantity on-hand for the case cart will be decremented and the quantity on-hand for the disposable items will be incremented. The quantity on-hand for reusable items will not change.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP CC ENTER/EDIT DEFINITION</td>
<td colspan="3">Enter/Edit/Create A Case Cart</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">CASECART^PRCPCED0</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Allows user to define which items and quantity should be used in assembling the case cart. The user can also enter special instructions or remarks for the case cart.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP CC LINK OPCODES</td>
<td colspan="3">Link Operation Codes to Case Carts</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">OPCODES^PRCPCED0</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Allows user to link operation codes to specific case carts. When a patient is scheduled for an operation code, the system will recommend the case carts that should be ordered.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP CC MENU</td>
<td colspan="3">Case Cart Menu</td>
<td>M</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">This is the main menu for the primary and secondary inventory point case cart system.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP CC OPCODE-CC LINK REPORT</td>
<td colspan="3">Operation Code-Case Cart Link Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPCROC</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Produces the Operation Code-Case Cart Link Report. The report lists selected case carts displaying the operation codes linked to the case cart. Includes the case cart description, item master number, the inventory point which the case cart should be ordered from, and the current quantity on-hand.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP CC/IK LOCATOR REPORT</td>
<td colspan="3">Specific Item Or Instrument Kit Locator Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPCRLO</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Produces the Specific Item Or Instrument Kit Locator Report, which indicates which case carts contain a specified item or instrument kit and which instrument kits contain a specified item. Includes case cart or instrument kit, the inventory point which created the case cart or instrument kit and the quantity needed to assemble the case cart or instrument kit.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCPLO CLO GIP OPTION</td>
<td colspan="3">CLO GIP Reports (CLRS)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="2">ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">ENT^PRCPLO3</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="2">DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6"><p>Each month, routines are scheduled to run the data extracts associated with PRC*5.1*83 (CLRS). As part of this run, the VMS flat files for both the Procurement and GIP extracts are created for FTP transmission. This routine handles the GIP data extracts, while routine PRCHLO5 handles the Procurement extracts.</p>
<p>This is the option used by the Prosthetics and Clinical Logistics Office to gather GIP information. It runs the Stock Status Report and Days of Stock on Hand Report for every combination of station and active inventory point present within a system and creates extracts in the CLRS REPORT STORAGE file (#446.7).</p>
<p>These extracts are "*" delimited files and encompass data extracted from the first day of the previous month to the last day of the previous month. The extracts are stored in the CLRS REPORT STORAGE file (#446.7) until the FTP transmission to the CLRS occur as instructed by the Prosthetics and Clinical Logistics Office</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCPLO CLO MENU</td>
<td colspan="3">Clinical Logistics Office Menu</td>
<td>M</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">N/A</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">This option is the Menu of all Clinical Logistics Office (Chief Logistics Office) options attached to the IFCAP Application Coordinator [PRCHUSER COORDINATOR] menu.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCPLO CLO SYSTEM PARAM</td>
<td colspan="3">CLO System Parameters (CLRS)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="4">ENT^PRCPLO4</td>
<td>LOCK:</td>
<td colspan="2">XUPROG</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">This option presents the user with the current value for the system parameters associated with PRC*5.1*83 (CLRS) and prompts them to enter new values if needed. Entries are screened for validity and any setting errors are returned to the user. <strong>This option is only intended to be used by IRM staff and access to it is restricted to those who have the XUPROG key.</strong></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<span id="_Ref106418957" class="anchor"></span>Table 6.34. Option List (PRCP COMPREHENSIVE — PRCP DUEOUT)

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 10%" />
<col style="width: 0%" />
<col style="width: 34%" />
<col style="width: 0%" />
<col style="width: 18%" />
<col style="width: 7%" />
<col style="width: 20%" />
<col style="width: 8%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th colspan="3">NAME</th>
<th colspan="4">Menu Text</th>
<th>Type</th>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<th colspan="2"></th>
<th colspan="6">Entry Action / Exit Action / Lock / Routine</th>
</tr>
<tr class="header">
<th colspan="2">DESCR:</th>
<th colspan="6">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP COMPREHENSIVE ITEM REPORT</td>
<td colspan="3">Comprehensive Item Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRCOM</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Prints a comprehensive listing of items within the inventory point.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP CONVERSION FACTOR REPORT</td>
<td colspan="3">Conversion Factor Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRCFR</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Produces the Conversion Factor Report. The report displays the inventory point items with procurement sources and conversion factors. Includes the item master number, description, NSN, unit per issue, quantity on-hand, procurement sources, unit per receipt and conversion factor. The Warehouse will have the option to select specific item NSNs to display, and the report is sorted by NSN. The Primary and Secondary will have the option to select specific group categories to display, and the report is sorted by group category and description.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP CONVERT SECONDARY</td>
<td colspan="3">Convert Secondary to Primary</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="4">PRCPCSP</td>
<td>LOCK:</td>
<td colspan="2">PRCP MGRKEY</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Converts an existing Secondary inventory point into a Primary. The Secondary must be a distribution point for the Primary most recently selected. Existing stock and reorder levels may be preserved. Existing PROCUREMENT SOURCES and the MANDATORY SOURCE (if present) in the secondary being converted will be replaced with the corresponding fields from the existing primary that supplies it. It is anticipated that this option will be used most frequently in conjunction with linkage of multiple primaries to a single FCP.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP COPY PRIMARY TO SECONDARY</td>
<td colspan="3">Copy Primary To Secondary</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPECPP</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Copies all items from a Primary inventory point to any Secondary inventory point managed by the Primary.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP COPY SECOND TO SECOND</td>
<td colspan="3">Copy Secondary To Secondary</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPECPS</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Copies all items from one Secondary to another Secondary inventory point managed by the same Primary inventory point.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP COST TREND ANALYSIS</td>
<td colspan="3">Cost Trend Analysis Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRCTA</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Produces the Cost Trend Analysis Report. The report computes the average item cost for the specified period based on the monthly opening balance last receipt cost. It will compare the computed average item cost with the current monthly opening balance average cost and display the percent increase or decrease change. The report includes the item master number, description, NSN (for Warehouse), unit per issue, cumulative average cost, current month average item cost, and percent change. It will break out each month and year in the selected date range and display the last cost opening balance. The user will have the option to specify the date range which should be used in computing the average item cost. The user can also specify which items to display and to print only a summary of the report. If the user selects to print only a summary, the report will not break out each month and year on the report. The Warehouse can select specific NSNs to display and the report is sorted by NSN. The Primary and Secondary can select specific item master numbers to display, and the report is sorted by description. The Primary will have the option to select specific group categories to display; the report is sorted by group category and description.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP DATE RECEIVED DELETE</td>
<td colspan="3">Date Received Delete (for Issue Book Requests)</td>
<td>E</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Allows user to delete or change the "DATE RECEIVED" field on a request. This field should be set only when the final partial on a request has been received, and is a flag to the system that no more receiving is due. If the user has accidentally specified that an order was received complete when it was not, the user can delete this field, and will then be allowed to receive more on the request.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP DAYS STOCK ON HAND REPORT</td>
<td colspan="3">Days Of Stock On Hand Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRSOH</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Produces the Days Of Stock On Hand Report. The report shows the item master number, description, NSN (for Warehouse), unit per issue, total usage for the period, average usage per day, current quantity on-hand, number of days of quantity on-hand remaining, and the total selling value of stock on hand. The total selling value of stock on-hand is shown at the end of the report. The Warehouse will have the option to select specific item NSNs to display and the number of days stock on-hand. Items which are greater or less than the specified number of days stock on-hand will be printed. The Warehouse report is sorted by NSN. The Primary and Secondary will have the option to select specific group categories to display and the number of days stock on-hand. Items which are greater than or less than the specified number of days stock on-hand will be printed. This report is sorted by group category and description.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP DIETETIC COST REPORT</td>
<td colspan="3">Dietetic Cost Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRDCR</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Produces the Dietetic Cost Report, which lists items received into specified inventory points. The report is sorted by selected inventory point, food group (from the Item Master File), NSN, and selected date received.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP DISPLAY ITEM</td>
<td colspan="3">Display Item</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRIT0</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Produces a comprehensive item report for a selected item stored in the inventory point or a selected item stored in a distribution point.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP DIST COST EDIT</td>
<td colspan="3">Distribution Costs Enter/Edit</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">EDIT^PRCPUCC</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Allows the costing data displayed on the "History of Distribution Report" (see PRCP DIST HISTORY REPORT) to be entered or changed.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP DIST HISTORY REPORT</td>
<td colspan="3">History Of Distribution Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRPDH</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Produces the History Of Distribution Report, which shows the distribution history to or from the inventory point by cost center and by MIS costing section.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP DIST ORDER LIST TO/FROM</td>
<td colspan="3">List Distribution Orders To/From Inventory Points</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRLDO</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Displays the distribution orders which have not been posted from the primary to the secondary inventory point. Allows the Primary to print the picking tickets for all orders which have been released, but have not had a picking ticket previously printed. The user has the option to print the orders with or without a breakout of the items on the order.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP DIST ORDER PRIM DUEOUTS</td>
<td colspan="3">Calculated Due-Out Quantity Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRDOR</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Prints a list of due-outs from the distribution orders. A user with the manager key will also have the option to update the inventory point with the calculated quantity due-out.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP DIST ORDER PROCESSING</td>
<td colspan="3">Distribution Order Processing</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPOPL</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">This is the main option for entering, releasing, and posting distribution orders from the Primary inventory point to the Secondary inventory point.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP DIST ORDER SECOND DUEINS</td>
<td colspan="3">Calculated Due-In Quantity Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRDOR</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Prints a list of due-ins from the distribution orders. A user with the manager key will also have the option to update the inventory point with the calculated quantity due-in.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP DUE-IN ITEM REPORT</td>
<td colspan="3">Due-In Item Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRDIN</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7"><p>Produces the Due-In Item Report showing the inventory point items which have outstanding transactions stored (in the inventory point) as due-ins. Includes the outstanding transaction, associated purchase order, vendor, estimated delivery date or partial numbers not received in, and the due-in quantity.</p>
<p><em>Note:</em> The results of this report may not agree with the report generated by the option "Update Calculated Due-Ins/Outstanding Transactions" (see PRCP DUEIN CALCULATE/UPDATE), because the "Update" option report shows the <em>calculated</em> due-ins, not the <em>stored</em> due-ins. If the "Update" option is run and the update is performed, the "Due-In Item Report" option can be run again and will then agree with the "Update" report, since the "Update" option will store the calculated due-ins.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP DUEIN CALCULATE/UPDATE</td>
<td colspan="3">Update Calculated Due-Ins/Outstanding Transaction</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPRDI0</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7"><p>Use to print a report showing the calculated due-ins, or to update the inventory point with the calculated due-ins. The calculated due-ins are based on transactions (2237's) and purchase orders which have not been received in after a specified date. The date entered should represent the date the last transaction or purchase order was received in (probably no later than 6 to 9 months in the past). The report should be run before doing the update so the results can be verified first. The report will show a listing of the calculated due-ins compared to the total due-in quantity stored in the inventory point. If the due-ins disagree, the update should be performed.</p>
<p><em>Note:</em> The report may not agree with the "Due-In Item Report" (see PRCP DUE-IN ITEM REPORT), since the "Due-In Item Report" uses the stored values and not the <em>calculated</em> values. The update will remove all due-ins stored in the inventory point and reset the due-ins to the newly calculated values.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP DUEOUT/OUTST TRAN CLEAN</td>
<td colspan="3">Clean Up Old Transactions And Due-Outs</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPWDOU</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7">Use to recalculate the due-outs from the Warehouse inventory point for issue book requests not posted. The due-out quantity is calculated from issue book request ordered after a specified date. The date selected should be the date the last issue book request has <em><strong>not</strong></em> been posted (probably 6 to 9 months in the past). All issue book request before the specified date will be made final and can no longer be selected for posting. The due-out quantity stored in the inventory point will be updated to the newly calculated due-out quantity. This option should be run at <em><strong>night</strong></em> since it will lock the transaction (2237) file, and Services will be unable to create <em><strong>any</strong></em> orders. After the option has calculated the due-outs, a report will print displaying the outstanding issue book request, line item numbers due-out, date of the request, primary inventory point making the request, and the outstanding due-out quantity.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP DUEOUT/OUTST TRAN REPORT</td>
<td colspan="3">Outstanding (Due-Outs) Transaction Listing</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="7">PRCPWDOR</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="7"><p>Use to recalculate the due-outs from the warehouse inventory point for issue book requests not posted. The due-out quantity is calculated from issue book requests which have not been posted to the primary inventory point. This option should be run at <em><strong>night</strong></em> since it is computer processing unit (CPU)-intensive. After the option has calculated the due-outs, a report will print displaying the outstanding issue book request, line item numbers due-out, date of the request, primary inventory point making the request, and the outstanding due-out quantity.</p>
<p>The report will also show the warehouse quantity on-hand and stored quantity due-out compared to the total calculated quantity outstanding (due-out). If the quantity due-out and the quantity outstanding disagree, the "Clean Up Old Transactions And Due-Outs" (see PRCP DUEOUT/OUTST TRAN CLEAN) option should be used.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<span id="_Ref106418963" class="anchor"></span>Table 6.35. Option List (PRCP EDIT — PRCP I\*)

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 10%" />
<col style="width: 0%" />
<col style="width: 34%" />
<col style="width: 0%" />

<thead>
<tr class="header">

<th colspan="3">Menu Text</th>
<th>Type</th>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">

<th colspan="5">Entry Action / Exit Action / Lock / Routine</th>

<tr class="odd">

<td colspan="2">Enter/Edit Items On Distribution Point</td>

</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPEITD</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Allows a warehouse or primary inventory point to update information on selected items for a distribution point. In order to select a distribution point, the distribution point must not be maintaining their inventory items.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP EDIT INVENTORY ITEMS</td>
<td colspan="2">Enter/Edit Inventory Item Data</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPEILM</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Allows items to be added, deleted, or changed within the inventory point. This is the main option for keeping the inventory items up to date. When using this option, an item may be selected up-front followed by the field types to edit, or, the field types to edit may be selected first followed by the inventory items to edit.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP EDIT MASTER ITEM FILE</td>
<td colspan="2">Master Item File Edit</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPE441</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Used to edit the fields in the Item Master File which are used by the SPD inventory point for case carts and instrument kits.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP EMERGENCY STOCK REPORT</td>
<td colspan="2">Emergency Stock Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPREME</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Prints a report of inventory point items which the quantity on-hand is at or below the emergency stock level. The report shows the unit per issue, normal stock level, emergency stock level, quantity on-hand, quantity due-in, quantity due-out, and interval order point. The report also shows the due-in transactions and associated purchase order number, vendor, estimated receiving date, and the due-in quantity. After the report has printed, the message "You have items at or below the emergency stock level" will be cleared.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP FMS REBUILD/RETRANSMIT</td>
<td colspan="2">FMS Code Sheets Rebuild/Retransmit</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPSFR0</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Used to rebuild and retransmit the FMS code sheets (IV and SV) from the Generic Code Sheet stack file.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP GRAPH USAGE</td>
<td colspan="2">Graph Usage</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPRGRA</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Displays a graph of usage for the past 13 months for selected items.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP GROUP CATEGORY EDIT</td>
<td colspan="2">Group Category Enter/Edit</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPEGRP</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Allows the manager of an inventory point to change or remove group categories which have been set up for the inventory point.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP IK ASSEMBLE</td>
<td colspan="2">Assemble Instrument Kit</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPCASK</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Used to build selected instrument kits by the instrument kit definition (which describes the items and quantities which are used in building the instrument kit). The user will have the option to select the number of instrument kits to build. After selecting the number, a screen display will show the current quantity on-hand and new quantity on-hand (after building) for the items which make up the instrument kit definition. The new quantity on-hand is calculated by subtracting the current quantity on-hand by the quantity needed for disposable items (reusable items are not removed from the inventory point during assembly). If any item's new quantity on-hand falls below zero, a warning message will be displayed on the screen.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP IK DEFINITION REPORT</td>
<td colspan="2">Instrument Kit Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPCRDK</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Produces the Instrument Kit Report. The report lists selected instrument kits displaying the items and quantities needed to assemble the instrument kit. Includes the items needed, description, quantity needed, whether the item is reusable or disposable, mandatory source vendor for reordering, catalog number for the mandatory source, and storage location.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP IK DISASSEMBLE</td>
<td colspan="2">Disassemble Instrument Kit</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPCDIK</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Used to disassemble (break down) instrument kits and return the individual disposable items back to stock. When an instrument kit is disassembled, the quantity on-hand for the instrument kit will be decremented and the quantity on-hand for the disposable items will be incremented. The quantity on-hand for reusable items will not change.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP IK ENTER/EDIT</td>
<td colspan="2">Enter/Edit/Create A Instrument Kit</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">INSTRKIT^PRCPCED0</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Allows user to define which items and quantity should be used in assembling the instrument kit. The user can also enter the method of sterilization, method of wrapping/packaging, and special instructions or remarks for the instrument kit.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP IK MENU</td>
<td colspan="2">Instrument Kit Menu</td>
<td>M</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">This is the main menu for the Primary and Secondary inventory point instrument kit system.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP INACTIVE ITEMS REPORT</td>
<td colspan="2">Inactive Items Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPRIIR</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Produces the Inactive Items Report. The report shows items which have not been used (distributed) and not received into the inventory point within a specified time period. Includes the last usage date, last receipt date, and due-out quantity. If the item is marked "DELETE ITEM WHEN INVENTORY 0," the quantity on-hand will also be displayed. The user is presented with a prompt to include or exclude Zero Quantity items in the report.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP INFORMATION REPORTS MENU</td>
<td colspan="2">Informational Reports Menu</td>
<td>M</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Contains the reports which will provide information on items stored in the inventory point.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP INQUIRE FILE ENTRIES</td>
<td colspan="2">File Inquiry</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPRINQ</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Allows user to inquire on VA FileMan file entries. The option will display selected entry data on the screen for the user to review.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP INV CONTROL PARAM PRINT</td>
<td colspan="2">Inventory Control Parameters Print</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPRINV</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Prints the control parameters for the inventory point or a selected distribution point. The parameters include the number of items stored in the inventory point, the cost center, fund control points, inventory point users (showing managers), distribution points, and any user classified as ODI manager (ODI MGR).</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP INVENTORY MENU</td>
<td colspan="2">Inventory File Maintenance Menu</td>
<td>M</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ENTRY:</td>
<td colspan="4">K:$G(PRCP("DPTYPE"))'="P" PRCP S PRCP("DPTYPE")="P" D DISPLAY^PRCPUSEL I '$G(PRCP("I")) S XQUIT=1 D NOMENU^PRCPUSEL</td>
<td>EXIT:</td>
<td>N/A</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">This menu includes the options for a Primary to maintain the items stored in the inventory point.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP INVENTORY SALES REPORT</td>
<td colspan="2">Inventory Sales Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPRISR</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6"><p>The Inventory Sales Report will print the item master number, description, nsn (for whse), date issued, quantity sold, selling cost, and total value sold.</p>
<p>The warehouse will have the option to select specific item nsn's and distribution points to display. The user can also specify the issue date range for sales. The report will sort by distribution point and nsn.</p>
<p>The primary will have the option to select specific distribution points and the issue date range for sales. The report will sort by distribution point and description.</p>
<p>The secondary has the option to select specific recipients and the date range. The report will sort by recipient and item description.</p>
<p>Additionally, the user of any of these reports has the option to print a summary of the report data. By printing the summary, the report will eliminate the print of each item and only print the total sales to selected distribution points or recipients.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP INVPT PARAM ENTER/EDIT</td>
<td colspan="2">Enter/Edit Inventory And Distribution Points</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPENLM</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">Allows the inventory point manager to edit the control parameters for the inventory point and distribution points. The control parameters include the cost center, fund control points, inventory point users, distribution points, etc.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP ISMS BALANCE TASKMAN</td>
<td colspan="2">TaskMan Sends ISMS Balance Update</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">TASKMAN^PRCPSMB0</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">This option can be set up through TaskManager to automatically send the ISMS Balance Update Transaction at a specified time. This ISMS transaction will send a snapshot of the current warehouse inventory balances to ISMS. ISMS will use the balances contained in this transaction to overlay the current ISMS balances.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP ISMS BALANCE UPDATE</td>
<td colspan="2">Balance Update Transaction (IM-6)</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPSMB0</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="6">This ISMS transaction sends a "snapshot" of the current warehouse inventory balances to ISMS. ISMS will use the balances contained in this transaction to overlay the current ISMS balances.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<span id="_Ref106418990" class="anchor"></span>Table 6.37. Option List (PRCP PURGE — PRCP SUBSTITUTE)

</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th colspan="3">NAME</th>
<th colspan="7">Menu Text</th>
<th>Type</th>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<th colspan="2"></th>
<th colspan="9">Entry Action / Exit Action / Lock / Routine</th>
</tr>
<tr class="header">
<th colspan="2">DESCR:</th>
<th colspan="9">Description</th>
</tr>

<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCP PURGE AUTOMATIC RUN</td>
<td colspan="5">Inventory Automatic Purge Taskman Option</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">DQ^PRCPXALL</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">This option is controlled by TaskManager. This option should be set up to run the first day of each month starting around 1:00am.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCP PURGE DISTRIBUTION HIST</td>
<td colspan="5">History By Cost Center Purge</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPXDIS</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Used to purge the Distribution/Usage History totals by cost center, for the month specified by the user. This file is used to create the month-end distribution report used by accounting.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCP PURGE MENU</td>
<td colspan="5">Purge History Files Menu</td>
<td>M</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ENTRY:</td>
<td colspan="8">D DISPLAY^PRCPUSEL I '$G(PRCP("I")) S XQUIT=1 D NOMENU^PRCPUSEL</td>
<td>EXIT:</td>
<td>N/A</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Contains options allowing the user to purge various history files, in order to free up disk space.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCP PURGE RECEIPTS HISTORY</td>
<td colspan="5">Receipts History By Item Purge</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPXREC</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Used to purge the receipts history for items stored in the inventory point. This option should be run once a month and will purge stored data which is older than 13 months. The data is used in the report</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCP PURGE TRANS REGISTER</td>
<td colspan="5">Transaction Register Purge</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPXTRA</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Used to purge the transaction register for all transactions which affect the inventory point that are older than 13 months. This option should be run once a month in order to free up disk space. The data is used for printing the inventory transaction register report.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCP PURGE USAGE/DISTRIBUTION</td>
<td colspan="5">Usage/Distribution Monthly Totals Purge</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPXUSE</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Used to purge the usage/distribution totals for items stored in the inventory point and are older than 13 months. This option should be run once a month in order to free up disk space. The data is used in the various "Usage Reports."</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCP QUANTITY DISTRIBUTION</td>
<td colspan="5">Quantity Distribution Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPRQDR</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10"><p>Produces the Quantity Distribution Report. The report presents a comparison between the normal stock level (entered by the user) and the calculated average stock distributed for the past year. This report will help in making adjustments to the stock levels (temporary, emergency, and normal). Provides a breakout of the quantity distributed by month, which will help in determining usage trends for items. The report includes the item master number, description, NSN (for Warehouse), unit per issue, standard reorder point, optional reorder point, temporary stock level, emergency stock level, and normal stock level. The Warehouse will have the option to select specific item NSNs to display, and the report is sorted by NSN. The Primary will have the option to select specific item master numbers to display; that report is sorted by description. The secondary will have options similar to the primary but the report will</p>
<p>display recipients instead of distribution points.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCP RECEIVE ISSUE BOOK ORDER</td>
<td colspan="5">Receive Issue Book Order</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPWPPL</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Used by the Primary inventory point to receive in issue book requests distributed by the warehouse. When receiving in the issue book request, the Primary on-hand quantity and due-in quantity is adjusted. The Warehouse quantities are not changed until the Warehouse posts the issue book request. If the Warehouse <em>has</em> posted the issue book request, the Primary will not be able to receive the order in since the Primary receiving process was done during Warehouse posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCP RECEIVE PURCHASE ORDER</td>
<td colspan="5">Purchase Order Receiving To Inventory Point</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPPOLM</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Used for receiving from any source <em>other than</em> Supply Warehouse (Issues). User enters a PO and the partial number received. For recurring items, the process updates inventory quantity. The process also recalculates the average unit cost for the item, based on a weighted average between the quantity on hand at the old average price, and the quantity received at a new price. It also updates the last unit cost, and the date last received, as well as receiving history showing the date and quantity received, and the percentage of normal stock level on hand before the receipt was posted to the inventory. If the user has specified that a detailed inventory transaction history should be kept, this file is also updated. For nonrecurring items, the process updates only the distribution history for the inventory point receiving the item.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCP RECEIVING/DISTR MENU</td>
<td colspan="5">Receiving And Distribution Menu</td>
<td>M</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ENTRY:</td>
<td colspan="8">K:$G(PRCP("DPTYPE"))'="P" PRCP S PRCP("DPTYPE")="P" D DISPLAY^PRCPUSEL I '$G(PRCP("I")) S XQUIT=1 D NOMENU^PRCPUSEL</td>
<td>EXIT:</td>
<td>N/A</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Contains all the options related to receiving and distribution in an inventory point.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCP REMOVE SS FROM DIST ORD</td>
<td colspan="6">Remove Supply Station From Dist Order</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">REMFLAG^PRCPOPR</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">This option will only be used when the interface between GIP and the supply stations is down for a long time. It allows the user to identify an individually orders that will be processed further in GIP and not by the supply stations.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP REPLACE ON-HAND INVENTORY</td>
<td colspan="6">Adjust Quantity to Supply Station Values</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="6">PRCPSSQT</td>
<td><strong>LOCK:</strong></td>
<td colspan="3">PRCPSSQOH</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">This option enables an authorized user to request that the quantities of items in the inventory point are adjusted to the quantities reported by the linked supply station at the time the request is made.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCP REPORTS MENU</td>
<td colspan="5">Reports Menu</td>
<td>M</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ENTRY:</td>
<td colspan="8">K:$G(PRCP("DPTYPE"))'="P" PRCP S PRCP("DPTYPE")="P" D DISPLAY^PRCPUSEL I '$G(PRCP("I")) S XQUIT=1 D NOMENU^PRCPUSEL</td>
<td>EXIT:</td>
<td>N/A</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Contains reports which can be used by the primary inventory point to manage and track item data.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP SS QTY DISCREPANCIES</td>
<td colspan="6">Supply Station Quantity Discrepancies</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPRDIS</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">This option will produce a report of all items whose on hand quantity differs from the on hand quantity last reported by the supply station. The option is only meant to be run by secondaries linked by supply stations.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCP STOCK STATUS REPORT</td>
<td colspan="5">Stock Status Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPPOLM</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Produces the Stock Status Report. The report provides a summary of all issues, receipts, and adjustments with the opening and closing balances by account codes. It will calculate the turnover rate, inactive item percent, long supply percent. All inventory points will have the option to select the specified month and year for the report. Also, users can enter the item inactivity cutoff month and year. Items which have not had activity after the specified cutoff date, will be used to calculate the inactive item percent on the report.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCP STORAGE LOCATION EDIT</td>
<td colspan="5">Storage Location Enter/Edit</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">

<td colspan="10">PRCPESTO</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">

<td colspan="10">Allows the manager of an inventory point to change or remove storage locations which have been set up for the inventory point.</td>

<tr class="odd">

</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPESTO</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Produces the Substitute Listing Report. The report includes the item master number, description, NSN, unit per issue, quantity on-hand, and substitute items. The warehouse will have the option to select specific item NSNs to display. The report is sorted by NSN.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="6">PRCP SUPPLY STA ORDER BUILDER</td>

</tr>
<tr class="odd">

<td colspan="10">SSS^PRCPAGSS</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">This option will be activated only through the Task Manager and will control the effort to automatically generate a distribution order for all secondary inventory points linked to a supply station.</td>
</tr>

<td colspan="7">K:$G(PRCP("DPTYPE"))'="S" PRCP S PRCP("DPTYPE")="S" D DISPLAY^PRCPUSEL I '$G(PRCP("I")) S XQUIT=1 D NOMENU^PRCPUSEL</td>

<td colspan="10">This is the main menu for the surgery users. It allows surgery users to tie operation codes to specific case carts and instrument kits. It also allows the surgery user to quickly complete orders to SPD for scheduled surgical procedures.</td>

<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCP SURGERY ORDER</td>

</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPCSOR</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Allows a Surgery user to quickly place orders to SPD for scheduled operation procedures. The Surgery user can specify the patient and scheduled operation. If there are case carts tied to the operation, the user can quickly release the order to SPD and the picking ticket will automatically print in SPD.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCP TRANSACTION REG REPORT</td>
<td colspan="5">Transaction Register Report</td>

<tr class="even">

</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Produces the Transaction Register Report . The Register stores all transactions which affect the inventory, for a specified month-year. User can select a single item, multiple items, or all items stored in the inventory point.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCP TRANSACTION REG REPORT</td>
<td colspan="5">Transaction Register Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPCSOR</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Produces the Transaction Register Report . The Register stores all transactions which affect the inventory, for a specified month-year. User can select a single item, multiple items, or all items stored in the inventory point.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="6">PRCP UNDO CONVERSION</td>
<td colspan="4">Undo a Secondary to Primary Conversion</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="5">EN^PRCPCSPX</td>

D ^PRCPUSEL S:'$G(PRCP("I")) XQUIT=1 S XQMM("J")="PRCP MAIN MENU"</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Reverses ("undoes") a conversion from Secondary to Primary. That is, the inventory point will become a Secondary once again. All inventory parameters, stock levels, reorder points, procurement sources, and MIS costing sections will automatically be restored to whatever they were immediately prior to conversion. The inventory point will also be reconnected with its former Primary.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCP UNIT COSTING REPORT</td>
<td colspan="5">Unit Costing Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPRCOS</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Produces the Unit Costing Report. The report lists items stored in the inventory point, showing the item information, unit per issue, SKU, average cost, last cost, and unit cost. This report can be used to verify the correct costing information in the warehouse.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCP UPDATE SUPPLY STA ITEMSR</td>
<td colspan="6">Supply Station Item Update</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">INIT^PRCPHLFM</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10"><p>This option will build transactions for supply station secondaries, that will be sent to its associated supply station. Transactions will be created for all items in the selected inventory point whose normal stock level is greater than zero. All transactions will be flagged as either</p>
<p>item adds or item edits, as specified by the user of this option.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCP USAGE DEMAND ANALYSIS</td>
<td colspan="5">Usage Demand Analysis Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPRUS1</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Produces the Usage Demand Analysis Report. The report shows the decrease or increase in usage for items stored in the inventory point. The report will compare a selected month-year to a range of dates (from month-year to month-year) and print the increase or decrease (specified) percentage change (also specified) for the period. The report will show the quantity used in the comparison month, the average quantity used per month for the date range, and the percent increase or decrease in usage. The report will sort from low percent usage to high percent usage. User will be able to select display items in specific group categories; STANDARD; ON-DEMAND; or ALL ITEMS.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCP USAGE DEMAND ITEM REPORT</td>
<td colspan="5">Usage Demand Item Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPRUSE</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10"><p>Produces the Usage Demand Item Report. The report shows the reports the usage/distribution within a specified date range of a single item, a set of selected items or of all items stored in the inventory point within a specified date range. User will be able to select display items in specific group categories; STANDARD; ON-DEMAND; or ALL ITEMS.</p>
<p>The report can be sorted by NSN (warehouse) or group category (primary or secondary inventory points) with the items in each category sorted either numerically or alphabetically. The report shows item information, unit per issue, last cost, average cost, used month-year, quantity used, total cost, and cumulative quantity and cost totals for each item in the date range.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="5">PRCP VOUCHER SUMMARY REPORT</td>
<td colspan="5">Voucher Summary Report</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPRVSR</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Produces the Voucher Summary Report. The report can be used to reconcile the warehouse inventory point for the month.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="5">PRCP WHERE ITEM STOCKED REPORT</td>
<td colspan="5">Display Where An Item Is Stocked</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="10">PRCPRSTK</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="10">Prints a report showing which inventory points stock a specified item. The report includes the distribution point, quantity on hand, and unit per issue. A field labeled 'OD' is displayed when the item is classified as ON-DEMAND.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<tr class="odd">

<td colspan="5">Auto-generate Orders</td>
<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">PRCPAGS0</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9"><p>Use this option to auto-generate a Secondary inventory point distribution order. The auto-generation will use the selected Primary distribution points (stored in the mandatory or suggested source field in the secondary) for selecting the items. When an item's available quantity (quantity on hand plus quantity due-in minus quantity due-out) falls below or equal to the standard reorder point, the item will be ordered. When an item's available quantity falls below or equal to the optional reorder point, the item will be ordered if there are other items for the same vendor which are being ordered due to the available quantity falling below the standard reorder point (if items only fall below the optional order point for a vendor, the order will not be generated). The quantity to order is the difference between the available quantity and the normal stock level. Conversion factors (primary to secondary), primary minimal issue quantity, and primary issue multiple also factor into the total quantity of an item to order.</p>
<p>At completion of auto-generation, a series of reports can be generated. Each item in the inventory point will appear on one of the reports. This will aid in determining why an item was or was not ordered.</p></td>
</tr>

<tr class="even">

<td colspan="9">Allows a user to transfer a barcode program from the host computer to the barcode reader and send scanned data back from the reader to the barcode file.</td>

<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="4">PRCT COMMENT ALIGNMENT</td>

<td>R</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ROUTINE:</td>
<td colspan="9">COM^PRCTBAR</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DESCR:</td>
<td colspan="9"><p>Allows the alignment of comments in a barcode program. Comments can also be aligned by using the FileMan programmer 'Y' option during the edit function. By executing the following code, comments can be aligned at any column for a range of lines:</p>
<p>S Y=[column] D CON^PRCTBAR</p>
<p>For example, while editing a barcode program, to align comments at the 28th column for lines 20-40:</p>
<p>At the "EDIT Option:" prompt, enter YES.</p>
<p>Then enter "S Y=28 D CON^PRCTBAR." FileMan then asks for the range of lines to process. Enter the range from 20 through 40, and those lines will have comments aligned at column 28.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="4">PRCT DATA MANAGER</td>
<td colspan="5">Data Manager Menu</td>
<td>M</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">

<td colspan="9">This menu handles the options that are needed to manage data that has been collected from a barcode reader.</td>

<td colspan="4">PRCT DESIGN LABEL</td>

</tr>

<td colspan="9">PRCTRED</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">

<td></td>
<td colspan="4">RUN FAIL, RTN IS MISSING</td>
<td colspan="5">Routine (446.4,.04) is not on system</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td></td>
<td colspan="4">STARTED AT JUL 07,1989@14:52</td>
<td colspan="5">Data has started processing at specified time</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td></td>
<td colspan="4">FINISHED ON JUL 07,1989@15:31</td>
<td colspan="5">Data finished processing at specified time</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td></td>
<td colspan="9"><p>The above status give the ability to view the progress of data from the point of when it was uploaded from the barcode reader to the time it has been processed. Certain status are errors (such as RUN FAIL and DEVICE NOT SELECTED); these mean the data will never be processed because of an unexpected error in the process.</p>
<p>The normal progression of status that data will take is:</p>
<p>1) ATTEMPTING DATA UPLOAD<br />
2) DATA UPLOAD SUCCESSFUL<br />
3) TASKED FOR [date/time]<br />
4) STARTED AT [date/time]<br />
5) FINISHED ON [date/time]</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<td>PRCHQ 864 NORMAL</td>
<td>Reporting arrival of 864 Text Message for review.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>PRCOEDI ACKNOWLEDGE</td>
<td>Receipt of a POA transaction</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>PRCP_ALL_ITEMS_QTY_UPDATE</td>
<td><p>alerts staff to the receipt to a QOH request. If</p>
<p>any quantity discrepancies are found between the items in the supply station</p>
<p>and those in the inventory point, they will be listed.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>PRCP_BAD_ACTIVITY</td>
<td><p>This bulletin alerts staff of problems in HL7 transactions that</p>
<p>update a secondary inventory point with supply station activity.</p>
<p>Problems include: item not on this inventory point, quantity is too large or too small, inventory point not in GIP.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>PRCP_BAD_ITEM_QOH</td>
<td>This item will display when GIP receives a QOH response from the supply station containing an item not in file 441.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>PRCP_BAD_ORDER</td>
<td><p>This bulletin alerts staff of refill activity that cannot be</p>
<p>processed because the transaction information conflicts with system data or data requirements.</p>
<p>Problems include: item not on the order specified, order not for the secondary specified, amount refilled inappropriate, HL7 transaction corrupted, order number specified is not in GIP</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>PRCP_BAD_QUERY</td>
<td>This message alerts users when a response to a quantity on hand query could not be processed by GIP.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>PRCP_ITEM_NAME</td>
<td><p>Alerts staff in a secondary inventory point of item name</p>
<p>discrepancies between the inventory point and the linked supply station.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>PRCP_NO_REFILL</td>
<td><p>This bulletin alerts staff that a posted distribution order</p>
<p>includes items that were not marked as refilled by the supply station. It is expected that staff will verify the correct refill amount for these items by creating another order of emergency or call-in to correct discrepancies resulting in both the primary and secondary inventory points.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>PRCP_ORDER_NOT_GENERATED</td>
<td>This message alerts staff expecting an order to be autogenerated for an inventory point that the order was not generated.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>PRCP_ORDER_PARTIALLY_LOST</td>
<td><p>This message will be sent to the secondary inventory point</p>
<p>managers when a supply station has reported refills against a distribution order but has not completed it. The purpose of the message is to notify staff of possible inconsistencies in the on-hand quantity between the supply station and the secondary.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>PRCP_QTY_MISMATCH</td>
<td><p>This bulletin will notify the secondary inventory staff of</p>
<p>inventory inconsistencies between the inventory point and its associated supply station. Staff need to investigate these discrepancies and make the necessary adjustments.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>PRCVUP</td>
<td>This bulletin will notify the FMS mail group that an entry in their VENDOR file has been updated by FMS. They will see both the original data and what has been changed.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>PRC_IFCAP_CHANGE</td>
<td>This bulletin will be used to notify users that there has been a change to a PO to allow updating the inventory point.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>PRCV_AUDIT_FILE_ERROR</td>
<td>This bulletin will be used to notify users that there has been an error while processing a DynaMed-related data item.</td>
</tr>

# Archiving and Purging

<!-- back-to-toc -->[↑ Table of Contents](#table-of-contents)

## Introduction

<!-- back-to-toc -->[↑ Table of Contents](#table-of-contents)

The IFCAP Archive/Purge (PRCG) program (see Table 6.14. Option List (PRCG)) allows IRM, Fiscal, and A&MM to manage the size and availability of the dated records in the IFCAP database. The package allows the systematic identification, archival, and removal of documents from File 442 and associated files from the VistA database.

The basic unit of the package is the document. A document is defined as the key entry in File 442 (PO, 1358, etc.) and all associated records in that and other files (amendments, adjustments, receiving reports and 2237 requests). During the archive these individual records are assembled and written out to the archival media (tape/HFS file) in printable format. These files may then be converted to microfiche for storage/retrieval. Automatic reinsertion into the VistA database following purge is not available.

## Overview of PurgeMaster

<!-- back-to-toc -->[↑ Table of Contents](#table-of-contents)

PurgeMaster is a utility designed to allow multiple processes to act on different aspects of a database simultaneously. In the past, record purging required a single job to process through and delete records one at a time. PurgeMaster allows the IRM service to determine the time and computing resources to be made available to the purge process. Some activities (for example, archiving) must be accomplished sequentially (that is, you can't write record two until record one is finished). Other activities can theoretically have multiple processes, with each chipping away at a portion of a job in parallel. The purging process fits this model very well. Up to three parallel purge processes appear to run efficiently.

This utility is designed to provide purging functionality in the background. While PurgeMaster can be invoked during the day to process with only one job, it is best used processing 3-5 background jobs during off-hours.

TaskManager normally initiates PurgeMaster daily. It monitors the IFCAP PURGEMASTER WORKLIST file (File 443.1) to determine if "killer" jobs need to be spawned to process transactions. The IFCAP PURGEMASTER WORKLIST file (File 443.1) gets entries by manual interaction of user personnel.

## Technical Information

<!-- back-to-toc -->[↑ Table of Contents](#table-of-contents)

### Namespace

<!-- back-to-toc -->[↑ Table of Contents](#table-of-contents)

The IFCAP Archive/Purge routines are contained in the namespace PRCG.

### Sizing Requirements

<!-- back-to-toc -->[↑ Table of Contents](#table-of-contents)

The Host file or MailMan disk space required for archiving appears to be about 40k per document archived. No real space is required when archiving to tape.

### System Failure during Archiving or Purging

<!-- back-to-toc -->[↑ Table of Contents](#table-of-contents)

If the system fails during archive, recreate the archive tape; if during purge, restart the job.

## Options

<!-- back-to-toc -->[↑ Table of Contents](#table-of-contents)

Any user with appropriate menus can run Archive/Purge. Because the archive writes to devices not normally accessed by non-IRM users, however, the expected user is an IRM employee working closely with the IFCAP Application Coordinator. Set-up of IFCAP Archive/Purge parameters is the responsibility of IRM. Coordination and approval for archive/purge is the responsibility of Fiscal/A&MM employees with the actual implementation being undertaken by IRM. The IRM user must be designated as an Authorized Fiscal User for at least one site and FISCAL ACCOUNTING AUTOMATED (Field 22 of File 411) must be set to YES.
